purpose: Formative development reference outcome for testing symptom-category fallback when a business-critical service function is unavailable but no more specific technical cause is directly supported.

incident_summary_requirements: State that most new customer sign-in attempts are failing across the United Kingdom and Ireland storefronts.
State that existing authenticated sessions continue to function.
Do not state or imply a confirmed downstream, platform, credential or configuration cause.

severity.rationale: A business-critical authentication function is unavailable to most signed-out customers across two storefront regions, but the incident is confined to one service and existing sessions continue to operate. The workaround position remains unknown.

incident_category.rationale: The directly supported condition is loss of an essential service function, while no more specific application, infrastructure, dependency or configuration failure has been identified.

affected_area.rationale: The Identity and Access Service is the visible affected technical area; all named supporting components are explicitly healthy.

routing.rationale: RG-IAM owns the Identity and Access Service. RG-OPS coordination is not required because the impact is limited to one service and is not Critical.

prohibited_recommendations: declare a credential or dependency failure without evidence

information_gaps: It has not been confirmed whether every authentication path and client type is affected.
No approved sign-in workaround has yet been confirmed for signed-out customers.

assessment_notes: This scenario deliberately withholds a specific technical cause so that CAT-AVAILABILITY is the correct bounded classification.
Healthy supporting components must not be selected as affected areas.
The two reported unknowns must be preserved as information gaps.
A structurally valid result must still be compared with this reference outcome for semantic correctness.
